docs.title: scc_utility
docs.text:
SCC Utility — automate SCC tasks for cdFMC/FTD.

Usage:

scc_utility [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

Options:

  API Credentials: [all_or_none]
    --region TEXT                 SCC region identifier (e.g., eu, us, ...).
    --api-token TEXT              SCC API access token. If omitted, you may be
                                  prompted at runtime.
  --help                          Show this message and exit.

Subcommands

  • deploy: Deploy pending changes to a single FTD.
  • deploy-all: Deploy pending changes to all online FTDs in the tenant.
  • deploy-bulk: Deploy pending changes to multiple FTDs at once.
  • list-versions: List compatible software versions for a given FTD.
  • monitor-upgrade: Monitor a bulk upgrade transaction until completion.
  • upgrade: Upgrade a single FTD device.
  • upgrade-bulk: Upgrade multiple FTD devices in bulk.

docs.title: deploy
docs.text:
Deploy pending changes to a single FTD.

The device can be selected by --ftd-uid or by name with --ftd-name. If neither is provided, an interactive selector is shown.

Examples: # Deploy by UID scc_utility deploy --ftd-uid 123456

# Deploy by device name (fuzzy match)
scc_utility deploy --ftd-name NKA-123456

Usage:

scc_utility deploy [OPTIONS]

Options:

  --ftd-uid TEXT   The UID of the FTD to deploy changes to.
  --ftd-name TEXT  Name of the FTD to deploy changes to (alternative to UID).
  --help           Show this message and exit.

docs.title: deploy-all
docs.text:
Deploy pending changes to all online FTDs in the tenant.

The command will: * Discover all devices of type CDFMC_MANAGED_FTD with state ONLINE. * Prompt twice for confirmation (safety check). * Trigger a bulk deploy if confirmed.

Examples: # Deploy to all devices (with confirmation prompts) scc_utility deploy-all

Usage:

scc_utility deploy-all [OPTIONS]

Options:

  --help  Show this message and exit.

docs.title: deploy-bulk
docs.text:
Deploy pending changes to multiple FTDs at once.

Prompts interactively to select multiple online FTD devices and then triggers a bulk deploy operation.

Example: scc_utility deploy-bulk

Usage:

scc_utility deploy-bulk [OPTIONS]

Options:

  --help  Show this message and exit.

docs.title: list-versions
docs.text:
List compatible software versions for a given FTD.

If --ftd-name is provided, resolves the UID automatically. Otherwise, falls back to interactive selection if no --ftd-uid is given.

Args: ctx: Click context with base_url and api_token. ftd_uid: Optional UID of the target FTD. ftd_name: Optional device name to resolve UID from.

Usage:

scc_utility list-versions [OPTIONS]

Options:

  --ftd-uid TEXT   The UID of the FTD to list compatible versions for.
  --ftd-name TEXT  The name of the FTD to list compatible versions for.
  --help           Show this message and exit.

docs.title: monitor-upgrade
docs.text:
Monitor a bulk upgrade transaction until completion.

Polls the SCC API at regular intervals and prints a live table of device upgrade status. Intended for use during bulk firmware upgrades.

Args: ctx: Click context object (must contain base_url and api_token). transaction_id: ID of the transaction to monitor. poll_interval: Interval in seconds between status polls (default: 2.0).

Usage:

scc_utility monitor-upgrade [OPTIONS]

Options:

  --transaction-id TEXT  The id of the transaction to monitor  [required]
  --help                 Show this message and exit.

docs.title: upgrade
docs.text:
Upgrade a single FTD device.

Performs optional deploy before upgrade and prompts the user to confirm before proceeding.

Args: ctx: Click context with base_url and api_token. ftd_uid: UID of the target FTD. upgrade_package_uid: UID of the package to upgrade to. ftd_name: Optional device name to resolve UID automatically.

Usage:

scc_utility upgrade [OPTIONS]

Options:

  --ftd-uid TEXT              The UID of the FTD to upgrade.
  --upgrade-package-uid TEXT  The UID of the upgrade package to use to perform
                              the FTD upgrade.
  --ftd-name TEXT             The name of the FTD to list compatible versions
                              for.
  --help                      Show this message and exit.

docs.title: upgrade-bulk
docs.text:
Upgrade multiple FTD devices in bulk.

Devices can be specified interactively or via an Excel file of references. Ambiguous matches are resolved interactively unless --non-interactive is provided.

Args: ctx: Click context with base_url and api_token. upgrade_package_uid: UID of the upgrade package (prompted if omitted). devices: Path to Excel file with device references. sheet: Optional Excel sheet name. column: Optional column name. non_interactive: If true, skip prompts and ignore ambiguous matches.

Usage:

scc_utility upgrade-bulk [OPTIONS]

Options:

  --upgrade-package-uid TEXT  The UID of the upgrade package to use to perform
                              the FTD upgrade.
  --devices XLSX              Path to an Excel file containing device names /
                              references (default column: 'devices')
  --sheet TEXT                Excel sheet name to read from (default: first
                              sheet).
  --column TEXT               Column name to read device references from
                              (default: auto; prefers 'devices').
  --non-interactive           Do not prompt to resolve ambiguous matches; skip
                              ambiguous rows instead.
  --help                      Show this message and exit.

docs.title: SCC Utility CLI User Guide
docs.text: This guide provides an in-depth overview of the scc_utility command-line interface (CLI), which automates common Security Cloud Control (SCC) tasks such as deploying and upgrading Firepower Threat Defense (FTD) devices, and monitoring upgrade transactions.

docs.title: Table of Contents
docs.text:
1. Overview
  2. Prerequisites
  3. Installation
  4. Authentication and Configuration
  5. Global Options
  6. Command Reference
  7. deploy
  8. deploy-bulk
  9. list-versions
  10. upgrade
  11. upgrade-bulk
  12. monitor-upgrade
  13. Interactive Mode
  14. Examples
  15. Troubleshooting
  16. Best Practices

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The scc_utility CLI simplifies and centralizes operations against the Security Cloud Control (SCC) APIs:

  • Deploy pending configuration changes to one or more FTD devices
  • List available and compatible firmware versions
  • Upgrade FTDs individually or in bulk
  • Monitor upgrade transactions in real time

All commands share a common entry point (app.py), invoking subcommands for each operation.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Windows OS (Windows 10 or later)
  • Access to the Netteam-Globalconnect GitHub organization (invite required)
  • Valid SCC API token with permissions to query inventory and perform deployments/upgrades

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
1. Download the latest MSI installer from the SCC Utility GitHub Releases page (requires a GitHub account and membership invitation): https://github.com/Netteam-Globalconnect/scc_utility/releases/latest
  2. Run the downloaded .msi file and follow the on-screen prompts to install the application.
  3. After installation, the scc_utility CLI tool will be available in your Start menu or via the command prompt.

docs.title: MSP Management
docs.text:
For MSP (Managed Service Provider) users, the CLI offers dedicated tenant management workflows:

  1. Tenant Selection: On startup, if your API token belongs to an MSP account, you’ll be prompted to select one of your managed tenants from the MSP portal.
  2. API-Only User Provisioning: The CLI ensures an API-only user exists in the selected tenant and, if not, provisions one automatically.
  3. Tenant-Scoped Token Generation: A fresh, tenant-scoped API token is generated for that API-only user and used for all subsequent operations.
  4. Seamless Context: After selection, all commands (deploy, upgrade, etc.) run in the context of the chosen managed tenant.

If no managed tenants are found, the CLI falls back to using your original API token and operates at the root level.

Before executing any commands, you must supply your SCC API credentials. You can provide them via:

  • Command-line options (--region, --api-token)
  • Interactive prompt (you’ll be prompted if neither option is set)

Credentials are managed by the SccCredentialsService, which caches or prompts to ensure secure handling.

docs.title: Global Options
docs.text:
All subcommands inherit these global options:

Option Description Required Example --region SCC region identifier No* eu --api-token SCC API access token (string) No* ABCDEF12345

*If omitted, you will be prompted at runtime or credentials loaded from cache.

docs.title: Command Reference
docs.text: Below is a detailed breakdown of each available subcommand.

docs.title: deploy
docs.text:
Syntax: 

scc_utility deploy [OPTIONS]

Description: Deploys any pending configuration changes to a single FTD device.

Options:

Option Description Required --ftd-uid UID of the target FTD No --ftd-name Name filter for selecting the FTD (prefix match) No

Behavior: 1. If --ftd-name is provided and matches exactly one device, its UID is used. 2. If multiple devices match or neither --ftd-uid nor --ftd-name given, an interactive selector appears. 3. Deploys with default notes: "Deployment via CLI". 4. Prints a success message on completion.

Exit Code: - 0 on success - Non-zero on failure

docs.title: deploy-bulk
docs.text:
Syntax: 

scc_utility deploy-bulk [OPTIONS]

Description: Deploys pending changes to multiple FTD devices in bulk.

Options: - (None) – all selection is interactive

Behavior: 1. Prompts to multi-select up to all online FTDs. 2. Deploys each device with a 1-second delay between calls. 3. Uses notes: "Bulk deploy from CLI".

docs.title: list-versions
docs.text:
Syntax: 

scc_utility list-versions [OPTIONS]

Description: Lists all firmware versions compatible with a given FTD.

Options:

Option Description Required --ftd-uid UID of the FTD No --ftd-name Name of the FTD (exact match) No

Behavior: 1. Resolves FTD via name or UID, or interactive selector if unspecified. 2. Fetches compatible versions via the DeviceUpgradeApiService. 3. Displays a table of versions, marking suggested versions with *.

docs.title: upgrade
docs.text:
Syntax: 

scc_utility upgrade [OPTIONS]

Description: Upgrades the firmware on a single FTD to a specified or selected version.

Options:

Option Description Required --ftd-uid UID of the target FTD No --ftd-name Name filter for selecting the FTD No --upgrade-package-uid UID of the upgrade package (firmware image) No

Behavior: 1. Resolves target FTD via name or UID; interactive if ambiguous. 2. If no upgrade package provided, prompts to select from compatible versions (suggested marked *). 3. Optionally deploys pending changes first (confirmation prompt). 4. Prompts for final confirmation before starting upgrade. 5. Executes the upgrade and prints status.

Interactive Prompts: - Select firmware version - Confirm pre-upgrade deploy - Confirm upgrade

docs.title: upgrade-bulk
docs.text:
Syntax: 

scc_utility upgrade-bulk [OPTIONS]

Description: Upgrades multiple FTD devices in bulk.

Options:

Option Description Required --upgrade-package-uid UID of the firmware package to apply No

Behavior: 1. If no package UID provided, interactive version selection. 2. Prompts to multi-select up to 10 online FTDs. 3. Upgrades all selected devices in parallel.

docs.title: monitor-upgrade
docs.text:
Syntax: 

scc_utility monitor-upgrade --transaction-id <ID>

Description: Continuously polls and displays the status of a bulk upgrade transaction.

Options:

Option Description Required --transaction-id ID of the transaction to monitor Yes

Behavior: 1. Polls every 10 seconds by default. 2. Renders a live-updating table of device states until completion.

docs.title: Interactive Mode
docs.text: Whenever a command cannot resolve a device or firmware version from provided flags, you will enter an interactive mode powered by questionary and rich. Use arrow keys and spacebar to navigate and select items.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Deploy to a specific device by UID: 

scc_utility deploy --ftd-uid a1b2c3d4 --region us-east-1 --api-token $SCC_TOKEN

Bulk upgrade with interactive version selection: 

scc_utility upgrade-bulk --region eu-west-1

Monitor an upgrade transaction: 

scc_utility monitor-upgrade --transaction-id tx-1234567890

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Authentication errors: Ensure your --api-token is valid and not expired. Re-run the command without --api-token to be prompted for fresh credentials.
  • Region not supported: Verify the region code is one of the supported regions in scc_utility/utils/region_mapping.py.
  • No devices found: Check that your SCC tenant has devices in an ONLINE state.
  • Bulk operations hanging: Use monitor-upgrade to inspect progress or failures.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Always run the deploy command before upgrading to ensure configuration consistency.
  • Review compatible versions with list-versions to confirm upgrade paths.
  • Use bulk commands for routine maintenance windows to minimize manual effort.
  • Automate monitoring by piping monitor-upgrade output into logs or alerting systems.

For further assistance, consult the project repository or contact the SCC support team.

docs.title: Cdfmc Api Service
docs.text:
CDFMC (Cisco Defense FMC) access policy utilities.

This module exposes a high-level service for interacting with the CDFMC configuration API to:

  • discover the active CDFMC domain (via the inventory API),
  • create a default Access Policy with a BLOCK default action,
  • add an Access Rule to block gambling URL categories,
  • look up common object IDs used by those operations.

It wraps raw HTTP requests (via :mod:requests) together with the scc_firewall_manager_sdk client objects to provide simple workflows that are used by the CLI and can also be reused programmatically.

Example 
from scc_firewall_manager_sdk import ApiClient, Configuration
from scc_utility.services.cdfmc_api_service import CdFmcApiService

with ApiClient(Configuration(host="https://example", access_token="...")) as api_client:
    svc = CdFmcApiService(api_client)
    policy_id = svc.create_default_access_policy()
    svc.block_gambling(policy_id)

docs.title: CdFmcApiService
docs.text:
High-level helper for CDFMC access policies and rules.

This service locates the CDFMC domain for the current tenant and exposes focused methods for creating a default Access Policy and adding an Access Rule that blocks gambling categories.

Attributes:

Name Type Description api_client

Initialized SDK client used for authenticated calls.

inventory_api

Convenience client for inventory lookups.

cdfmc_domain_uid

The discovered CDFMC domain UID to target.

Note

This service performs a domain lookup during initialization by querying device managers of type CDFMC. If none (or multiple) are found, initialization fails.

Example 
svc = CdFmcApiService(api_client)
policy_id = svc.create_default_access_policy()
result = svc.block_gambling(policy_id)

docs.title: create_default_access_policy
docs.text:
create_default_access_policy()

Create a default Access Policy with a BLOCK default action.

Returns:

Type Description str

The UID (id) of the newly created Access Policy.

Raises:

Type Description HTTPError

If the underlying POST request fails.

docs.title: block_gambling
docs.text:
block_gambling(access_policy_uid)

Add an Access Rule to block gambling URL categories.

The rule: * matches source network object any-ipv4, * blocks URLs categorized as Gambling with reputation TRUSTED_AND_UNKNOWN, * is created under the provided Access Policy.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default access_policy_uid str

Target Access Policy UID where the rule will be created.

required

Returns:

Type Description dict

The JSON body returned by the API for the created rule.

Raises:

Type Description HTTPError

If any underlying request fails.

RuntimeError

If required objects (e.g., any-ipv4) cannot be resolved.
